chunks: "When I charge a LiPo I watch four things: voltage, current, temperature and time, plus a few supporting signals. Voltage, per cell. Each cell must stay at or below 4.
20 volts, and in a series pack I watch the spread between cells. If one cell is racing ahead, that's imbalance, and the charger needs to balance or stop. Current.
In the constant-current phase it should sit at the set value, say 1C. In constant voltage it should fall smoothly. I terminate when it reaches about C over 20 to C over 10.
If the current doesn't taper, the cell has a leakage path or something is wrong. Temperature, from an NTC on the cell.
I want about 0 to 45 degrees for charging, and I also watch the rate of rise: a pack warming at a degree a minute during a gentle charge is a red flag.
A few degrees' rise at 1C is normal. Time: a safety timer, so if termination never happens the charge ends anyway.
And then the surroundings: the input voltage and current limit of the supply, the charger IC's own temperature, and physically, swelling, smell, hissing.
A healthy charge looks like a flat current, then voltage pinned at 4. 2, current decaying and temperature rising only a few degrees.
Anything else, a cell voltage that doesn't rise in precharge, current stuck in CV, a cell hot at low current, means stop and disconnect."
